hero.lead: A nation of 57.5 million that already makes four-fifths of its electricity from renewable sources, and still leaves two in five citizens below the poverty line.

capital.heading: Kenya has bought time. Next, the price.

record.text: Total public debt, 68.5% of GDP, end June 2026
External debt service paid in the year to June 2026
IMF Extended Fund and Extended Credit Facilities, approved April 2021; the programme ended in April 2025
Foreign direct investment in 2025, the highest on record

register.name: Dual-tranche Eurobond
register.note: US$900 million amortising 2032 to 2034; US$1.35 billion amortising 2037 to 2039
register.text: Part of the proceeds bought back US$90.5 million of the 7.250% notes due 2028 and US$324.8 million of the 8.000% notes due 2032; the rest supports the budget. Both coupons came in below the 9.5% Kenya paid a year earlier.

register.name: Dual-tranche Eurobond
register.note: Overall cost of 8.7%, as stated by the National Treasury
register.text: Raised to buy back part of the 7.250% notes due 2028 ahead of schedule. The Treasury put its cost nearly a full percentage point below the bond sold in February 2025.

register.name: Eurobond, amortising 2034 to 2036
register.note: Order book above US$5 billion
register.text: Issued to buy back debt falling due in 2027. Holders tendered US$579.7 million of the US$900 million 7.000% notes, leaving about US$320 million to repay in May 2027. It extended the maturity at a high price: 9.5% a year on a currency the nation does not print.

register.name: Infrastructure bond IFB1/2024/8.5
register.note: KSh 70 billion offered; KSh 288.7 billion bid
register.text: A shilling bond sold at home to fund infrastructure in the 2023/24 budget, amortised over its life and listed on the Nairobi Securities Exchange. Local savers lent more than three times the amount asked, in their own currency.

register.name: Eurobond, amortising 2029 to 2031
register.note: Refinanced the US$2 billion debut Eurobond due June 2024
register.text: Kenya came back to the market months before its first Eurobond fell due, and repaid that bond in full. It was the first of four liability operations since 2024 that pushed Kenya’s dollar repayments further out.

register.name: Second Kenya Fiscal Sustainability and Resilient Growth
register.detail: Approved June 2026 · Project P508021 · IBRD $340 million, IDA $410 million · Second of a series of three
register.note: Public finance, competitive markets and climate action
register.text: World Bank budget support for a Treasury Single Account, electronic procurement, payroll controls and faster capital grants to counties, and for regulations that run the Enhanced Single Registry of the National Safety Net Program. It also backs competition, technical training, refugee inclusion and a framework for sovereign sustainability-linked finance. It serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Horn of Africa Gateway Development Project, additional financing and second project
register.detail: Announced 27 March 2026 · IDA · $290 million additional financing and $260 million second project
register.note: 508 km of the Isiolo–Mandera corridor; Nairobi to Mandera in one day instead of three
register.text: Two World Bank operations that upgrade 508 km of the 740 km Isiolo–Mandera corridor and lay about 1,270 km of high-capacity fibre optic cable through remote, underserved areas of the northeast. Lower transport and trade costs support livelihoods and jobs, and serve the livelihood standard.

register.name: Second Kenya Social and Economic Inclusion Project
register.note: About 12 million people
register.text: Strengthens the social protection system that reaches the poorest households, and so works on livelihood: about two in three Kenyans live below the World Bank’s line of US$4.20 a day.

register.name: Extended Fund and Extended Credit Facilities
register.detail: Approved 2 April 2021 · Resilience and Sustainability Facility added July 2023 · Ended April 2025
register.note: Initial EFF/ECF commitment, later augmented
register.text: The programme that carried Kenya through the repayment of its 2024 Eurobond. The combined seventh and eighth reviews, concluded on 30 October 2024, released about US$485.8 million under the EFF/ECF and US$120.3 million under the RSF, and shifted access toward the zero-interest ECF. A successor programme is reported to be unlikely before the 2027 elections.

register.name: Secondary Education Equity and Quality Improvement Program
register.note: Paid on verified results
register.text: Widens fair access to good-quality secondary schooling and strengthens the systems around it.

register.name: First Kenya Fiscal Sustainability and Resilient Growth
register.detail: Approved 30 May 2024 · Development policy lending · IBRD $850 million, IDA $300 million, IDA grant $50 million
register.note: IBRD loan, IDA credit and an IDA grant for host communities and refugees
register.text: The first of a series of three World Bank policy operations, supporting reforms in public finance, markets and climate action while Kenya kept to its fiscal consolidation path. It helped Kenya meet the immediate fiscal pressures of 2024.

register.name: Building Resilient and Responsive Health Systems
register.note: $160m IDA, $40m refugee and host-community window, $15m Global Financing Facility
register.text: Aims to increase the use of primary healthcare, reduce the financial risk of illness and strengthen key health institutions. It is the operation aimed most directly at health, which scores 57 on the WHO index.

register.name: Kenya GREEN Program, Phase 2
register.note: Renewable imports and grid capacity
register.text: Raises renewable energy imports and the grid’s capacity to absorb variable renewable power.

register.name: Kenya Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene Program
register.note: Water and sanitation in selected counties
register.text: Expands water and sanitation access, aims to end open defecation, and improves the finances of water service providers.

register.name: Green and Resilient Expansion of Energy Program
register.note: To improve the financial viability of KPLC and increase access to electricity
register.text: Ties finance for the national utility to results on its accounts and on new connections.

register.name: Second Kenya Urban Support Program
register.note: Urban infrastructure and services
register.text: Builds the capacity of urban institutions to improve infrastructure and services, and supports refugee camps in becoming integrated settlements.

register.name: National Youth Opportunities Towards Advancement
register.note: Jobs, earnings and savings for young people
register.text: To increase employment, earnings and savings for targeted youth, at national scale.

register.name: Economic Inclusion and Green Recovery Support Programme, Phase II
register.note: Public finance, debt reporting, MSMEs, women and green growth
register.text: African Development Bank budget support for public financial management, fiscal transparency, debt reporting, procurement and financial integrity, and for small businesses, women’s economic empowerment and green growth. It builds on the first phase and serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Thwake Multipurpose Water Development Program, Phase I, additional financing
register.detail: Approved 22 May 2026 · AfDB €64.20 million and ADF €4.2 million · Completion due September 2028
register.note: Water for 1.3 million people, 40,000 hectares of irrigation, 20 MW
register.text: African Development Bank financing to raise the Thwake dam, strengthen its foundations and build two saddle dams, with about 90 percent of construction done. The dam is to supply up to 150,000 cubic metres of water a day to 1.3 million people and irrigate 40,000 hectares. It serves the water and food standards.

register.name: Support to Higher Education, Science and Technology Project, Phase II (HEST II)
register.detail: Approved 24 October 2025 · African Development Fund loan
register.note: 19 public universities; more than 20,000 students by 2030
register.text: African Development Fund financing for laboratories, equipment and digital learning in 19 public universities, three engineering centres of excellence and a science and technology park. It funds scholarships for 103 lecturers and incubation for more than 100 youth-led start-ups. It serves the education and livelihood standards.

register.name: Standard gauge railway loans
register.detail: Borrowed by June 2015 · Converted from dollars to yuan in 2025
register.note: Repayment now runs to 2040, after a four-year grace period
register.text: Three Export-Import Bank of China loans built the railway from Mombasa to Nairobi and Naivasha, at floating dollar rates above 6%. In 2025 the Treasury converted them to yuan at about 3%, which it says saves about US$215 million a year, and stretched the term to 2040.

register.name: OrPower Twenty-Two geothermal plant, Menengai
register.detail: Approval announced 22 January 2026 · 35 MW · Total debt $64.4 million, project cost $91.9 million
register.note: The third geothermal plant in the Menengai field
register.text: An African Development Bank loan for a 35 MW geothermal plant built by an independent power producer near Nakuru, with further IFC funding expected. It adds clean baseload power from the Rift and serves the energy standard.

register.name: KCB Bank Kenya green lending and trade finance
register.detail: Signed 11 December 2025 · $100 million subordinated debt · $50 million transaction guarantee
register.note: KCB aims for 25 percent green lending by 2031
register.text: African Development Bank Tier II capital for green loans in renewable energy, infrastructure and agriculture, and a guarantee that covers confirming banks on KCB’s letters of credit. It widens credit for firms that create jobs and serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Foreign direct investment
register.note: Record inflow, up from US$2.32 billion in 2024
register.text: All direct investment by foreign companies into Kenya in 2025, the highest on record, led by the digital economy and a data centre to run on geothermal power.

register.name: Lake Turkana Wind Power
register.note: The largest private investment in Kenya’s history
register.text: A wind farm in Marsabit, in the north, financed by eleven lenders under the lead of the African Development Bank, which used its first partial risk guarantee to close the deal. The Rift and the wind already pay their way.

register.name: Acorn green bond
register.note: Partial credit guarantee from GuarantCo
register.text: Kenya’s first green bond and first project bond, it financed green-certified student housing in Nairobi. It was listed in Nairobi and London, and repaid in full in 2024.

register.name: Kenya Mortgage Refinance Company notes
register.note: First tranche of a KSh 10.5 billion programme, oversubscribed more than fourfold
register.text: KMRC lends long-term, fixed-rate funds to banks and SACCOs so that home loans become cheaper and longer. Built on World Bank and African Development Bank credit lines, it then turned to the bond market.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Rift Heat
items.label: Geothermal capacity, FY 2024/25
items.text: Clean baseload power that runs day and night, whatever the weather. Few nations of any size own it.
items.alt: Geothermal steam rising from the Rift Valley in Kenya

items.name: The Clean Grid
items.label: Of electricity from renewables
items.text: Generation is still about 252 kWh a person a year, a quarter of the 1,000 kWh that Perfect Capita sets for every citizen. The grid is clean; it is not yet large.
items.alt: Wind turbines and power lines in Kenya

items.name: The Land
items.label: Of land in agriculture, 2024
items.text: Half the land is farmed, while more than a third of people are undernourished. The asset is under-used, not absent.

items.name: The Sea
items.label: Exclusive economic zone
items.text: About 640 km of coast and a narrow shelf, largely unmapped for finance.
items.alt: The Indian Ocean off the Kenyan coast

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: Young and growing fast: the 2019 census counted 47.6 million. One in three lives in a city.

items.name: SunCulture
items.text: Solar irrigation for smallholder farms, paid for as the crops grow.

items.name: Nairobi water ATMs
items.text: 257 prepaid taps in informal settlements, at KSh 2 for 20 litres.

items.name: Gjenge Makers
items.text: Paving bricks made from plastic waste and sand, in Nairobi.

items.name: M-KOPA
items.text: Solar and phones paid for in small daily sums; 4.8 million Kenyan customers since 2010.

items.name: Eneza Education
items.text: Lessons, quizzes and a live teacher by SMS, on any phone.

items.name: Penda Health
items.text: Nairobi clinics where an AI safety net cut diagnostic errors by 16%.

items.name: M-PESA
items.text: Mobile money that lifted 194,000 households above the poverty line.

coverage.gap_text: Kenyan children reach the end of primary school unable to read a simple text. Education is the standard furthest from reach.

guarantees.name: Food
guarantees.note: Not food insecure; 72% are moderately or severely food insecure

guarantees.name: Water
guarantees.note: Basic water; safely managed water is not measured

guarantees.name: Energy
guarantees.note: About 252 kWh a person a year, against 1,000; 32% cook cleanly

guarantees.name: Education
guarantees.note: 21% of children read a simple text by the end of primary school

guarantees.name: Livelihoods
guarantees.note: Above US$4.20 a day; 65% live below it

dispatches.label: 12 Oct 2026
dispatches.author: preeti
dispatches.title: Kenya has bought time. Now it should buy down the price.
dispatches.summary: Each liability operation has pushed Kenya’s dollar debt further out. None has made it cheaper. A guaranteed refinancing, with health, water and power targets written in, would.
